pages.text: This chapter goes over how QMD's fluids are used in Nuclearcraft's turbines and condensers to make power and recycle working fluids. It will not give details on how to construct turbines, heat exchangers or condensers, which are part of default Nuclearcraft.

pages.title: Mercury Cycle
pages.text: A $(l:multiblocks/vacuum_chambers/nucleosynthesis_chamber)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$(/l) heats hot mercury into high pressure mercury. This is a closed cycle, so once it is filled no new mercury is needed:$(li)1 mB hot mercury + 128 H makes 2 mB high pressure mercury$(li)In a turbine, 1 mB high pressure mercury makes 192 RF and 3 mB exhaust mercury$(li)In a condenser, 6 mB exhaust mercury makes 1 mB hot mercury

So each 128 H makes 384 RF, a base efficiency of 3 RF/H. The real efficiency also depends on how the turbine is built. The ideal expansion level for high pressure mercury is 3.$(br2)To start the cycle, feed the chamber plain mercury, which needs 256 H per mB instead of 128 H and makes the same 2 mB of high pressure mercury.

pages.title: Condensers
pages.text: Condenser recipes are shown in JEI. Exhaust mercury and hot mercury condense at 700 K and condensate water at 350 K. A condensation tube only works on sides that touch a colder fluid block, such as water at 300 K. Each such side adds a speed of $(l)κ(1+ln(Tc/T))$(), where $(l)κ$() is the tube's conductivity, $(l)Tc$() the condensing temperature and $(l)T$() the fluid block's temperature.

One recipe of 6000 mB exhaust mercury takes 2560 divided by that speed in ticks. A thermoconducting tube touching water on six sides has a speed of about 13.9, so it condenses about 32 mB/t. A large chamber makes thousands of mB/t of exhaust mercury, so expect to need hundreds of tubes.$(br2)Hot mercury can also be condensed into plain mercury if you want to empty a cycle.

pages.title: Water
pages.text: A $(l:multiblocks/other_multiblocks/liquefier)liquefier$(/l) cooled with water outputs condensate water. A condenser turns 1000 mB of this back into 1000 mB of water, which closes the loop. If you have plenty of water, you can dump the condensate water instead.

pages.title: Reactors
pages.text: Nuclearcraft's fission reactors can't heat mercury, so the mercury cycle only runs on a Nucleosynthesis Chamber. Molten salt reactors heat NaK, which a heat exchanger uses to make high pressure steam for a turbine. That is all default Nuclearcraft, and QMD doesn't change it.
